Quantifiers, Less, Little, Few
You can use little, few and less to talk about small quantities of something either countable or uncountable.
I want to include little color on this web page.
But little color can lead to the lack of interest in the web page, few people use neutral colors only on their designs.
Anyway, I will like to have less color than on previous designs.

To talk about small quantities for uncountable nouns you use little.
Structure:
Little + Noun + Complement
Example:
Little color can lead to the lack of interest in the design.

You can use Less as the comparative form of little.
Structure:
Statement + Less + Noun + Than + statement

Example:
I have less time than in the previous design to finish.

To talk about small quantities for countable nouns you use few.

Structure:
Few + Noun + Complement

Example:
Few colors should be implemented in this design.
Basic Color Theory
There are different color theories which are difficult to explain, yet there is one that involves all of the simple details and characteristics for color theory.
Well, it will be a different design; few people have tried that combination of colors, yet it will contrast with color harmony.

A perfect harmony will be the appropriate balance of analogous colors; they are side by side in a color wheel. Complementary colors; they are opposite colors like red and green. Nature scheme colors; they basically are yellow, red and green.

Basic color theory includes all of the aspects that are coherent and usable. These are color harmony and the color wheel.

Color harmony refers to the appropriate balance that should be presented in any design regarding colors. It must give a nice visual experience for the viewers.

The color wheel refers to a color circle which core colors are red, blue and yellow. Sir Isaac Newtown pioneered this color wheel in 1666. Basically, primary, secondary and tertiary colors appeared in sequence.

The main idea for color theory is that of creating a logical structure for colors.

Jeff : Hi Laura, what time does the meeting start?
Laura : Hey, Jeff! I think it starts around 11:00 am. Why?
Jeff: Well, I'm a little worried. We have a lot of work. For example, when are we working on the colors for the web page?
Laura: Hmm, I guess, we're working on that tomorrow morning. But don't worry, we can discuss about it while the meeting starts. Tell me, what are we going to do regarding color?
Jeff: Good idea! Well, I want to include little color on the web page. That's why I'm only going to use neutral colors.
Laura: But little color can lead to the lack of interest in the web page, few people use only neutral colors on their designs. You know, neutral colors are used as a backdrop in the designs. They serve to combine other colors, colors that are usually bright.

Jeff: I see. So, why don't we combine neutral and tertiary colors?
Laura: Tertiary colors?
Jeff: Yeah, colors that are formed by mixing warm and cool colors. You know, that's why the colors are given a two word name as red-orange, blue-green, red-purple, etc.
Laura: Well, it will be a different design; few people have tried that combination of colors. Furthermore, it will contrast with color harmony.
Jeff: Color harmony?
Laura: Color harmony is the appropriate balance of colors. It can evoke either a nice or terrible experience to the users.

Jeff: What will be a perfect harmony?
Laura: A perfect harmony will be the appropriate balance of analogous, complementary, and nature schema colors. Regarding analogous colors, they are side by side in a color wheel. Complementary colors are opposite colors like red and green. And, nature schema colors are basically yellow, red, and green.
Jeff: OK, so I think we are going to need to work on the combination of colors before we work on the draft. Anyway, I will like to have less color than on previous designs. You know, I want it to be different.
Laura: OK, I see your point. I'm sure we're doing a great job tomorrow. What time do you arrive at the office tomorrow?
Jeff: I arrive around 8:00 am. As soon as I arrive I'm going to your office.
